The driver should display good behaviour and be neatly dressed. Smoking and use of cell phone during driving by Driver is pro hibited. It is desirable that driver should wear proper neat and clean formal unif orm with shoes. 7. The contractor/agency participating in the tender should normally be GST co mpliant regarding registration, filing of returns etc., and shall be fully responsibl e for the compliance as per GST Act at all times. If the Contractor falls either “b elow the turnover threshold for GST” or is a “Composition Taxable Person” unde r the CGST Act, a self-declaration should be enclosed with his offer duly support ed by a certificate of turnover from a Chartered Accountant or enclose Form „R EG-06‟ showing as “Composition” under Type of Registration and no GST is applicable for contracts with such persons/firms. ost of fuel is included in the rate. Any further changes in GST regulations, in futur e, shall be adopted accordingly. 8. This agreement will not involve regularization of their service in Railways nor confer any right for appointment on the Railways 11. of new staff and if any deficiency in quality of service due to frequent change of staff is noticed, CMS/GTL may levy penalty of Rs.5000 per instance. 13. If any fine or penalty is imposed by various authorities such as RTA, Traffic Police etc for any violation such as speed, traffic rules violat ion etc, the same will have to be borne by the Contractor only. Scope of Service: The Scope of service deals with hiring of all-inclusive monthly basis Ambulance service ( including all expenses towards running of ambulance such as, but not limited to drivers salary, fuel requirements, maintenance, taxes and other expenses) of a Type B – Patient transport Ambulance that run on either pe trol or diesel, which are specially equipped and ergonomically designed for tran sportation /emergent treatment of sick or injured people and capable of providi ng out of hospital medical care during transit / when stationary, commensurate with its designated level of care when appropriately staffed. The duration of hire would be 24 months on 7 days a week and 24 hou rs basis. The ambulances provided should be CMVR approved and Automotive Industry S tandards – 125 (Part 1 & 2) compliant, Category M 4-wheeler vehicle, ergonomi cally designed, suitably equipped and appropriately staffed for the transport an d treatment of patients requiring non-invasive airway management / basic moni toring. Services for which hired ambulance will be used at HU/DMM : • Attending emergency calls from Employees at work place like departmental of fices, Diesel shed, Railway station, open lines and around Dharmavaram Town and Gunta kal division jurisdiction. • Attending emergency calls of Railway beneficiaries within Railway colonies an d Dharmavaram town limits.

• Transferring patient from HU/DMM to DRH/GTL (35Kms) or empanelled hospita ls at Kurnool (100Kms) or Anantapur (60Kms) or Hyderabad. • To attend Train accident relief services • Attending travelling passenger calls by medical team and if required for shifting passengers to HU/DMM or nearest Government Hospital in case of serious illness. • Conveyance of outstation patients to Railway station. • To transfer of Medicines and hospital related items from DRH/GTL to HU/DMM • To arrange first aid and as a standby medical service at various Railway Progr ammes. • To accompany the convoy of VIP visits. • For any other services of Medical Department on instructions of CMS/GTL or In charge Medical Officer/HU/DMM Service Details and Standards: 1. Proposed ambulance should be Single stretcher premium van of make similar to Tata Winger Ambulance 3200/3400 or Force Traveler Ambulance or SML Isuzu Ambulance or Tata 407 Ambulance or of similar make with manufacture year 2025 or after with trave lled up to 50,000Kms. 2. Ambulance deployed should confirm to the specifications with all-requisite fa ctory fitted accessories, tools, and accessories including spare wheels and the other equi pment in compliance as per AIS-125 of the National Ambulance Code and as per the M.

V.Act /Rules in force. The ambulance should preferably be of white color. 3. Constructional and Functional Requirements for Road Ambulance should be a s per AIS-125 (Part-1) of the National Ambulance Code and technical requirements for medi cal equipment should be as per AIS-125 (Part-2) of the National Ambulance Code and over t hat, specifications mentioned in this document. Other terms and conditions menti oned in Service level agreement for Monthly basis ambulance service in GeM are also applica ble. 4. Ambulance deployed shall have all the necessary permits/licenses/clearances such as, but not limited to fitness certificate, PUC, full comprehensive insurance (including th ird party, property and damage coverage), road permit, registration certificate as per the Motor Vehicles Act, RTO and other applicable laws and statutory bodies, for providing commercial vehicles for this service and should be registered with Transport department of Andhra Pradesh. 5. Ambulance should be in excellent working condition (both internally and exte rnally) at all times and should be cleaned thoroughly both internally and externally, boot k ept clear of dust, rubbish, oil, bad odor and any personal belongings of the driver.

6. The ambulance should ensure: a) minimum noise of engine and body while running b) tires with proper treads c) appropriately inflated stepney d) working headlights, tail lamps, indicators, speedometer, milometer etc. e) proper paint on the outside f) good condition of bumpers g) upholstery in good condition including washed and ironed white seat cove rs h) proper locking of all doors i) proper closing and opening of all windows. 7. Ambulance shall be available 24-hours of everyday in the week including Sun day and holidays parked at the premises of HU/DMM with full or sufficient tank of fuel availability. 8. In case the vehicle is not available due to any reason, the contractor must pr ovide another vehicle with similar model & facility and any low facility arrangements will not be acceptable. 9. In case of non-availability of the vehicle the CMS/GTL or Medical Officer/HU/D MM may arrange another vehicle and the expenditure incurred in this way would be re

covered from the monthly bill of the tenderer /bidder including initiating proper action. 10. In case of noncompliance of the standards of the services to be provided as per this agreement, CMS/GTL or Medical Officer/DMM would be at liberty to levy suc h penalty and terminate the contract as per the conditions detailed out in SLA of GeM. 11. Ambulances deployed cannot be taken-out of HU/DMM without written perm ission from CMS/GTL or Medical Officer/HU/DMM. 12. The front and rear wind screens should have a sticker reading “AMBULANCE ”. The Ambulance shall display a mark “ON SOUTH COAST RAILWAY DUTY” on the ambulance at his cost, for making the ambulance conspicuously distinguishable from a distance. 13. Any expenditure towards of wear and tear, repairing or regular servicing an d maintenance would be borne by the tenderer/bidder. 14. Hospital shall not be liable for any damage to vehicle during the course of use. 15. The legal liability arising out of Accident (whether on duty or off duty) if any, during the period of engagement would be managed and borne by the tenderer/bidder

. 16. Any loss of property or any other claim caused by the driver would be recov ered from the monthly bill of the tenderer/bidder. 17. The driver employed by the bidder should be under insurance cover of accid ent policy for loss of life/injury etc and compensation, if any this regard if awarded, will be the responsibility of the bidder. 18. The ambulance must have a dedicated working smart mobile connection for easy contact by Doctor’s, hospital staff or passengers. It must also have an active intern et connection at all times where google maps can be accessed, to navigate the shortest and / or fastest route possible avoiding traffic jams. The driver on duty shall be reachable at all ti mes through this mobile number. The driver should be sharing the live location by any m eans available when demanded by the hospital authority 19. Payment of all applicable statutory obligations such as minimum wages labo ur laws, tax laws etc. Rules are to be observed by the tenderer & hence all statuary liability viz. ESI/EPF etc would be solely borne by the tenderer/bidder and no extra payment wou ld be made on these account.

20. The Drivers should maintain logbook as prescribed format regarding movem ent of ambulance which will be certified by CMS/GTL or Medical Officer/HU/DMM o n start and end of each day and trip. Format of Log Book is in Annexure-I. 21. Patient cabin of the Ambulance should have following features: a) Patient cabin should be ventilated as required in accordance with the crit eria specified in AIS-125 (Part-1) of the National Ambulance Code b) Vehicle should have reinforced suspension system for providing to patient a Comfortable ride, free from external noise. c) Adequate power supply arrangements for medical equipment’s. d) Adequate patient cabin space for patient (In comfortable position), and s eat for at – least one attendant and two paramedics amenable for attending to the patient. e) Complete flooring free of joints suitable for easy cleaning /scientific/fumi gation and treatment with disinfectants. f ) Two (at least) superior quality fans and sufficient lighting arrangements a nd exhaust fan. g) Storage space for keeping medical equipment’s and consumables require d. h) Siren and beacon as per approved norms of govt.

i) A “No Smoking” sign will be prominently displayed in the patient compart ment. 22. List of Equipment to be made available in the Ambulance: a) Patient Handling Equipment 1. and oxygen reservoir – 1 Nos 8. Portable Suction Aspirator, Manual – 1 Nos c) Type of Diagnostic Equipment: 1. Manual B. P. Monitor Cuff Size: 10 cm. - 66 cm – 1 Nos 2. Cardiac Monitor with NIBP, ECG, Pulse Oximetry monitoring ISO 60601- 2-4 – 1 Nos Stethoscope – 1 Nos 3. Thermometer Minimum Range: 28oC to 42oC – 1 Nos 4. Device for Blood Sugar determination – 1 Nos 5. Torch Light – 1 Nos d) Type of Infusion Material or Equipment 1. Infusion Mounting- 2 Nos e) Other equipment’s: 1. Kidney Bowl – 1 Nos 2. Vomiting Bag– 1 Nos 3. Bed Pan – 1 Nos 4. Non-Glass Urine Bottle – 1 Nos 5. Sharps Container – 1 Nos 6. Waste Bags – 1 Nos 7. Medical waste Bags– 1 Nos 8. Non-Woven Stretcher Sheet – 1 Nos 9. Fire Extinguisher, ABC Type (minimum 2 kg capacity complying with IS: 13849 or IS:2171) 10. Nebulisation Device – 1 Nos 23. Drivers: a) The drivers of the ambulances must possess a valid driver license and mu

st have a minimum 2 years of driving experience. b) The Drivers should have the basic knowledge on First Aid and ABC resusc itation in case of medical emergencies. c) The drivers of the ambulance deployed should maintain polite & courteou s behaviour towards the Hospital staff/ passenger. “Misbehaviour” which may include , but not limited to, consumption of alcohol during or prior to duty, denial of duty during service hours as defined by user, use of abusive language, uncordial behaviour, t heft, shall attract penalties as per provisions of the contract. d) The Driver shall remain available all the times as per Duty Roster and sha ll not leave place of Duty from assigned Ambulances without prior permission of Hos pital authority. e) The driver should update about the trip status when demanded while in j ourney. 24. In the event of any dispute arising regarding the interpretation of any clause s of this agreement or in relation to the performance of this contract, the decision of the CMS/GTL shall be final. 25. The Contractor has to note that the services of the staff engaged by him will purely be on Contract basis. This agreement will not involve regularization of their servic

e in Railways nor confer any right for appointment on the Railways. 26. The contract for the vehicles hired can also be terminated with a short notic e of 15 days on account of unsatisfactory services at the discretion of the CMS/GTL. The uns atisfactory service shall mean and include the non-compliance of any of the obligations by the service provider, as given in this agreement and/or under the penalty clauses of the agreement or repeated breach. 27. Along with tender, bidders should be advised to enclose the list of ongoing v ehicle hire contracts with Railways, Other Central Government Departments,State Gov ernment and PSUs in the same city/location/ agglomeration with details of Contract Perio d, rate per month, Vehicle Class , Model and brand, Fuel (Diesel/Petrol/ LPG/CNG/Electri c/Hybrid), procurement cost (ex-showroom price) etc. Submission of this statement, ev en if Nil, shall be mandatory enclosure to the tender failing which the offer will be summari ly rejected. This is included so that tender committee may keep this additional data in vi ew while deciding the reasonableness of the offer received or to break the tie. 28. Labour Laws (Central/State) as applicable from time to time. The employees of the Contractor shall not be deemed to be employees of the user department/Rai lway. Hence the compliance of the applicable Acts/Laws will be the sole responsibility of the Contractor. 29. The contractor shall submit Police verification certificate for the driver empl oyed by him within 15 days of employment failing which he shall be levied a penalty of R s.200 per day for next 15 days after which the driver would not be allowed to work in abse nce of Police verification certificate. 30. The contractor must try to keep a designated team of drivers to work aroun d the shift with leave reserve. The contractor must avoid frequent employment of new staff and if any deficiency in quality of service due to frequent change of staff is noticed, C MS/GTL may levy penalty of Rs.5000 per instance. 31. The drivers employed be of minimum 10th Class qualification and not older t han 60years and possess valid Aadhar card which should be produced on demand. 32. The drivers employed by the contractor should always be wear proper neat and clean uniform with shoes and always possess ID card issued by the contact agenc y.

33. Cleanliness and sanitisation of Ambulance is the responsibility of tenderer/bi dder as per National Guidelines for Clean Hospitals by MoH&FW . As per point No:6.9 of the said guidelines, Ambulances should be cleaned by following below mentioned pr inciples: a) Routine clean following each transport: 1. Place biomedical waste (e.g., dressings, bandages, contaminated sheets t hat are saturated with blood) in a colour coded bins as per Biomedical Waste (Management and Handling) Rules 1998. 2. Remove used linens/ blankets for laundering. 3. Clean and disinfect/ sterilize equipment used during the call. 4. Clean and disinfect patient compartment as required. 5. Inaccessible areas should be vacuum cleaned. 6. If the vehicle is heavily contaminated it will be taken out of service and intensively cleaned. 7. Restock vehicle as required. b) Intense Cleaning as Required and When Scheduled: 1. Driver’s Compartment. 1. Remove all equipment from the front of the vehicle. 2. Clean and disinfect all interior surfaces, including walls, doors, radio e quipment, dash and windows. 2. Patient Compartment 1. Remove stretchers, clean and disinfect including mattress and belts; c heck for wear or damage.

2. Remove wall suction, clean and disinfect. 3. Remove contents of cupboards and shelves; clean and disinfect all sur faces. 4. Clean, disinfect and dry all hard surface items before returning to cup board or shelf; inspect for damage and expiration dates; repair/ replace as needed. 5. Sweep, vacuum, clean and disinfect floor. 6. Clean and disinfect chairs, bench seats, seat belts. 7. Clean and disinfect all interior surfaces, including ceiling and walls. 8. Check interior lighting. 9. Empty, clean and disinfect waste containers. 10. Clean interior windows. 3. Equipment Storage Compartment 1. Remove all equipment and sweep out compartment. 2. Clean and disinfect compartment and restock. 34. The Ambulance hired will be paid for a minimum run of 1500Kms per month as per agreement. But whenever the run kilometer’s is more than 1500Kms in the month, the excess Kilometers of 500/month may be allowed. Also upto 40% of total agre ed kilometer (40% of 1500 i.e 600Kms) is allowed by GeM and payment would be done as per agreed rate per Kms while accepting the Tender offer.

Scope of Service: The Scope of service deals with hiring of all-inclusive monthly basis Ambulance service ( including all expenses towards running of ambulance such as, but not limited to drivers salary, fuel requirements, maintenance, taxes and other expenses) of a Type B – Patient transport Ambulance that run on either pe trol or diesel, which are specially equipped and ergonomically designed for tran sportation /emergent treatment of sick or injured people and capable of providi ng out of hospital medical care during transit / when stationary, commensurate with its designated level of care when appropriately staffed. The duration of hire would be 24 months on 7 days a week and 24 hou rs basis. The ambulances provided should be CMVR approved and Automotive Industry S tandards – 125 (Part 1 & 2) compliant, Category M 4-wheeler vehicle, ergonomi cally designed, suitably equipped and appropriately staffed for the transport an d treatment of patients requiring non-invasive airway management / basic moni toring. 33. Cleanliness and sanitisation of Ambulance is the responsibility of tenderer/bi dder as per National Guidelines for Clean Hospitals by MoH&FW . As per point No:6.9 of the said guidelines, Ambulances should be cleaned by following below mentioned pr inciples: a) Routine clean following each transport: 1. Place biomedical waste (e.g., dressings, bandages, contaminated sheets t hat are saturated with blood) in a colour coded bins as per Biomedical Waste (Management and Handling) Rules 1998. 2. Remove used linens/ blankets for laundering. 3. Clean and disinfect/ sterilize equipment used during the call. 4. Clean and disinfect patient compartment as required. 5. Inaccessible areas should be vacuum cleaned. 6. If the vehicle is heavily contaminated it will be taken out of service and intensively cleaned. 7. Restock vehicle as required. b) Intense Cleaning as Required and When Scheduled: 1. Driver’s Compartment. 1. Remove all equipment from the front of the vehicle. 2. Clean and disinfect all interior surfaces, including walls, doors, radio e quipment, dash and windows. 2. Patient Compartment 1. Remove stretchers, clean and disinfect including mattress and belts; c heck for wear or damage.

2. Remove wall suction, clean and disinfect. 3. Remove contents of cupboards and shelves; clean and disinfect all sur faces. 4. Clean, disinfect and dry all hard surface items before returning to cup board or shelf; inspect for damage and expiration dates; repair/ replace as needed. 5. Sweep, vacuum, clean and disinfect floor. 6. Clean and disinfect chairs, bench seats, seat belts. 7. Clean and disinfect all interior surfaces, including ceiling and walls. 8. Check interior lighting. 9. Empty, clean and disinfect waste containers. 10. Clean interior windows. 3. Equipment Storage Compartment 1. Remove all equipment and sweep out compartment. 2.
